service.description: The current user's notifications, newest first, with their topic, inbox, reason, record, actor and app, and the counts the screens show beside them. Filters: inboxEnumId (NinNotifications by default; 'all' for both), reasonEnumId, appName, topic, topicList (any of these topics, for an app's own list), viewed (N unread, Y read, empty both), fromDate and thruDate (on sentDate), text (in the title, ignoring case) and approvals (only the approvals waiting: unviewed, of a topic with an approve service).

parameter.name: viewed
parameter.description: N for the unread, Y for the read, empty for both

parameter.name: message
parameter.description: The messageJson, parsed

parameter.name: unreadCounts
parameter.description: The unread of each inbox, by inboxEnumId

parameter.name: approvalCount
parameter.description: The approvals waiting

parameter.name: reasonCounts
parameter.description: The unread of the inbox by reasonEnumId ('' for none)

parameter.name: appCounts
parameter.description: The unread of the inbox by appName ('' for none)

service.description: Mark the current user's notifications viewed: those of notificationMessageIdList, or, without one, all of the user's unviewed, of one inbox when inboxEnumId is given, except the approvals waiting (notifications of a topic with an approve service), which are decided, not read. Only the user's own rows change.

parameter.name: notificationMessageId
parameter.description: One id, as a list of one

parameter.name: inboxEnumId
parameter.description: Without ids: NinNotifications or NinUpdates; empty for all

service.description: The current user's decision on a notification that asks for one (IronStone R23): the topic's approveServiceName is called, as the user, with recordEntityName, recordId, message (the messageJson as a Map) and notificationMessageId; its results are returned. The user must be a recipient (NotificationMessageUser). On success the decision is final for the message: every recipient's row is marked viewed, so it leaves the approvals waiting of all of them (an approval each of several users decides is a message per user); the service's errors are the caller's messages and nothing is marked.

As approve#NotificationMessage, with the topic's refuseServiceName, which also gets reason. When the topic has refuseReasonRequired=Y a refuse without a reason is an error; otherwise the refuse service decides whether it needs one.
The body of approve#NotificationMessage and refuse#NotificationMessage.

parameter.name: decision
parameter.description: approve or refuse

service.description: The daily digest (a ServiceJob): for each user who has the digest on for a topic (NotificationTopicUser.digest=Y, or NotificationTopic.digestDefault=Y and no user row that says N), one email of their unviewed notifications on those topics sent in the last hours, that no email carried yet (neither the immediate email of a topic the user gets by email, nor an earlier digest); each goes in one digest at most (NotificationMessageUser.digestDate). The job is hourly; a user is sent only in the hour of their NOTIFICATION_DIGEST_HOUR preference (0–23, missing means 6) in their time zone. A user who cannot be signed in (disabled, terminated) or has no email address is passed over; a failing user is logged and the others still get theirs.

parameter.name: ignoreHour
parameter.description: When true, send whatever the hour (a test). The scheduled job leaves this false.

parameter.name: userCount
parameter.description: The users a digest was sent to

parameter.name: notificationCount
parameter.description: The notifications those digests carried

service.description: One user's digest, for send#NotificationDigests: with nobody signed in (the job) the session takes the user's time zone and locale, so the dates are the user's (the machine's zone when the account has none); sends the template with notificationList, notificationCount, userId and userFullName as its body parameters; and sets digestDate (and emailMessageId, when the email is saved) on each NotificationMessageUser row it carried. Unless ignoreHour, it sends only when the local hour is the user's NOTIFICATION_DIGEST_HOUR (0–23, missing means 6), read from UserPreference by userId (the job is not signed in as them), and a skipped hour marks nothing. A disabled or terminated account gets none.

Whether this host can send Web Push (supported: built with the web-push feature), has its VAPID key (configured, with the publicKey a browser subscribes with, or unavailableReason), how many browsers the current user has subscribed (subscriptionCount), and whether the browser with endpoint is one of them (subscribed). Adds no error: a host without push answers supported false.

Store the current user's browser subscription (the PushSubscription's endpoint and its p256dh and auth keys, base64url). The endpoint must be https and the keys a P-256 point and 16 bytes. An endpoint stored before, for this user or another, becomes this user's and is enabled again, so a browser never gets another account's pushes after a sign-in. Refuses with an error when no user is signed in or push is not built.

Forget the current user's subscription with endpoint (the browser turned notifications off, or is signing out). Another user's endpoint is left as it is, with no error. Logout also deletes the subscriptions the visit stored.

Internal: run on a service worker when a persisted notification is sent, and for a call's ring and its end. Pushes title, link, topic and tag (the notification message id) to each active subscription and registration of userIdList. A browser's (PushWeb) is encrypted (RFC 8291) with a VAPID token (RFC 8292); a push service answering 404 or 410 disables it, as 5 failures in a row do. A native app's (PushFcm) goes by FCM's HTTP v1 API as a data message {kind: notification | ring | ringEnded, topic, tag; title, link; for a ring callSessionId, chatRoomId, caller, video, expiresAt; for a ring's end callSessionId, reason} (FCM reserves "from"), android.priority HIGH for urgency high, with ttl from ttlSeconds. FCM answering 404, UNREGISTERED, SENDER_ID_MISMATCH or a 400 about the token disables it; another 400 is logged as an error and leaves it. 429 and 5xx are tried again twice, never past a ring's end; then, as with no access token, the rest of the send is not tried and no device is counted against. One whose device key has ended is deleted. Each one fails on its own, logged by its id; FCM is skipped, with one info line in the log, while fcm_service_account is not set.

parameter.name: ttlSeconds
parameter.description: How long a push service keeps the push for a device that is offline, at most (and by default) a day: a call's ring passes on its ring time

parameter.name: urgency
parameter.description: normal (the default) or high (a ringing call)

parameter.name: callSessionId
parameter.description: A call's ring: the call, which makes the FCM message a ring (kind ring) for the app to show as an incoming call. Not in a Web Push payload.

parameter.name: chatRoomId
parameter.description: A ring: the call's room

parameter.name: fromName
parameter.description: A ring: the caller's name

parameter.name: video
parameter.description: A ring: whether it is a video call

parameter.name: expiresAt
parameter.description: A ring: when it stops ringing, in epoch milliseconds

parameter.name: kind
parameter.description: ringEnded (with callSessionId and reason): the ring of the call is over, for the apps' ring screens only; no Web Push is sent

parameter.name: reason
parameter.description: A ring's end: answered, declined, timedOut or ended

service.description: Keep the push registration of the native app this request comes from, for the current user: an FCM registration token (provider fcm, pushProviderEnumId PushFcm) or a UnifiedPush distributor's endpoint where the phone has no Google Play (provider unifiedpush, PushUnified; plans/Comms-Messaging.md §7.4), stored as a WebPushSubscription with the device key the request signed in with (its login_key header), and the app's push public key and auth secret (p256dhKey, authSecret: the Web Push keys, RFC 8291), which every push to it is encrypted with, so the push service reads nothing (§7.2 rule 5); a UnifiedPush registration needs them, an FCM one without them gets pushes with no text. Refused with an error unless the request was signed in by an unexpired device key of the user's (one with a deviceName), so the registration always ends with its device: revoke#UserDeviceKey or logout with revokeLoginKey deletes it, renew#UserDeviceKey moves it to the new key. A token stored before, for this user or another, becomes this registration and is enabled again; an older token of the same device key is replaced.

parameter.name: provider
parameter.description: fcm or unifiedpush

parameter.name: token
parameter.description: The FCM registration token, or the UnifiedPush endpoint (an https URL); no spaces, 4096 characters at most

parameter.name: p256dhKey
parameter.description: The app's P-256 push public key, base64url

parameter.name: authSecret
parameter.description: The app's 16-byte push auth secret, base64url

parameter.name: appId
parameter.description: The app's id, such as the Android package name

parameter.name: platform
parameter.description: android (the default)

service.description: Forget the current user's FCM or UnifiedPush registration with token, or with no token every registration of the device key this request signed in with. Another user's token is left as it is, with no error.
Whether this server sends FCM (fcmConfigured: fcm_service_account is set), and whether the device key this request signed in with has an enabled registration (registered). Adds no error.

The current user's device showed a push (plans/Comms-Messaging.md §7.3, Acknowledgement): ackId is a chat push's ackId (its PushOutbox id, in the encrypted payload), or the pushId a push of send#WebPush carries (the registration's id). The device's ackedCount and lastAckDate are kept (System, Push Health), and a chat push's ackedDate. acked is false, with no error, for a push that is not the user's. An acknowledgement means the device got the push, not that the person read the message.

A test notification to the calling device through the full path (plans/Comms-Messaging.md §7.6, the app's notification check): the chat push outbox, encrypted to the device, its push service. The device is the app of this request's device key, else the current user's browser with endpoint. ackIdList are the pushes queued (the device acknowledges each, ack#Push, and its check screen shows how long it took); empty, with reasonCode noDevice, for a request that is no push device of the user's, or tooSoon, for a device that had a test in the last 10 seconds (retryAfterSeconds). queuedDate is when, in Unix milliseconds.

Every user's push devices and how their pushes go (the PushHealthAdmin permission): each device {subscriptionId, userId, userName, providerText, platform, appId, userAgent, keyed (it gave its push keys), createdDate, lastRegisteredDate, lastPushDate (its push service took one), lastAckDate, sentCount, ackedCount, failedCount, failureCount (in a row), disabledDate, waitingCount (pushes pending or held), unackedCount (pushes sent between a day and ten minutes ago with no acknowledgement), acknowledges (it has acknowledged a push: an app that does, a browser with the acknowledging service worker), missedAcks (the alert: a device that acknowledges with unackedCount above 0; a device that never acknowledged is not alerted on)}, the devices with missed acknowledgements first, then the latest push; at most 500. With the totals: devices, waiting, failed in the last day, missed. The endpoint and keys are never returned.
